name: list_charts
description: List every chart type this server can draw: what it draws, how to fill `series` for it, which options apply, and a minimal example call for render_chart. Call this first when you are unsure which chart fits the data or how to shape `series`.

type.description: the chartType value to pass to render_chart
type.title: Type

summary.description: what the chart draws and when to use it
summary.title: Summary

series.description: how to fill `series` for this chart type
series.title: Series

options.description: render_chart options that affect this chart, beyond title/border/useColor which every chart accepts
options.title: Options

name: render_chart
description: Render numeric data as an ASCII/Unicode text chart. Supports sparkline, vbar, hbar, line, area, scatter, dual_axis, pie, histogram, heatmap, boxplot and dotplot, with an optional title, border frame (none/ascii/light/heavy/double/rounded), bar/area fill style (solid/halftone/ascii) and line style (solid/dotted), dashed reference lines (a threshold, or several labelled thresholds such as a target and an SLA) and configurable per-point markers for line charts, a target chart width (vbar/hbar scale to fill it), automatic diverging bars for negative values (including stacked), and optional ANSI 256-color output. Returns the chart as plain text — put it in a code block so it stays aligned. Use list_charts to see how `series` is filled for each chartType.

name.description: optional series/category/row name, used in legends and axis labels
name.title: Name

values.description: numeric values; meaning depends on chartType, see list_charts
values.title: Values

points.description: (x, y) samples, used only by scatter charts
points.title: Points

label.description: shown right of the plot next to the value, e.g. "target" or "SLA"
label.title: Label

series.description: one or more data series/rows/slices to plot; see list_charts for how each chartType reads them
series.title: Series

labels.description: category labels for vbar/hbar/histogram/dotplot bars, x-axis labels for line/area, or column headers for a heatmap
labels.title: Labels

title.description: optional title shown above the chart
title.title: Title

width.description: chart width in characters (default depends on chart type)
width.title: Width

height.description: chart height in rows (default depends on chart type)
height.title: Height

style.description: visual style. vbar/hbar/histogram/area: solid (default; flat blocks, bars end on whole character cells), fine (bars end on eighth-block glyphs for sub-cell precision; needs a font that has them, which Consolas does not), halftone (lighter stippled Unicode shades per series) or ascii (plain-ASCII characters per series — #, X, H, W, =, :, |, . then @ % & $ M N D O U S G Z / \ ! — that render identically in any monospace font). line: solid (default) or dotted (sparse plotted-dot trend line)
style.title: Style

stacked.description: for vbar/hbar/area with multiple series, stack them (cumulative from zero; negative values stack the other way) instead of grouping/overlaying
stacked.title: Stacked

bins.description: number of buckets for histogram charts (default: 10)
bins.title: Bins

useColor.description: ANSI 256-color output (default: auto, which is equivalent to off since tool output is plain text for an agent, not a terminal)
useColor.title: Usecolor

threshold.description: line charts only: draw a dashed horizontal reference line at this y-value
threshold.title: Threshold

thresholds.description: line charts only: several dashed horizontal reference lines, each named with its value right of the plot, e.g. [{"value": 106, "label": "target"}]
thresholds.title: Thresholds

showPoints.description: line charts only: mark each individual data point with a glyph on top of the connecting line
showPoints.title: Showpoints

pointChar.description: line charts only, with showPoints: single character used to mark points on every series (default: a large circle for the first series, with a distinct shape per additional series)
pointChar.title: Pointchar
